Project name: Lumineon Price Feed.
Application contract name: LumineonPriceFeed.

The purpose is to demonstrate that real IMD oracle attestations can update a card price onchain, where other contracts can read it. This is a testnet prototype.

1. Fixed card and pricing definition

The feed represents exactly:
- Lumineon V.
- English Pokémon TCG, Crown Zenith: Galarian Gallery.
- Card number GG39/GG70.
- Grading company PSA, grade 10.
- Currency USD, stored as an unsigned integer in cents.

The price means the headline price-guide estimate explicitly labelled “PSA 10” at:
https://www.pricecharting.com/game/pokemon-crown-zenith/lumineon-v-gg39

It is a published benchmark observation, not an individual sale, asking price, guaranteed resale value, or average across sources. Exclude shipping, taxes, and fees. Expose the card identity, denomination, and source through readable contract metadata.

2. Real IMD oracle integration

Follow the current IMD oracle documentation:
https://imd.fun/docs/

Use the current official OracleAttestation.sol implementation supplied by IMD where available, with the version-2 EIP-712 schema. Verify compatibility against IMD’s actual attestation format; do not invent a substitute signing format.

Pin the trusted IMD attester from the supplied network configuration. Verify the signature against this deployed consumer’s address and Sepolia domain. Validate the signed chain context according to the protocol.

Bind accepted answers to the exact approved card-and-pricing question using IMD’s actual question-hashing rules. Explain how repeated requests remain compatible. Do not let the first submitter choose the trusted question or signer.

Require a panel of at least 20, quorum of at least 14, and agreed count meeting the signed quorum, with internally consistent counts. Accept only correctly encoded, positive uint256 prices in cents. Reject conflicting answer and figure values.

Anyone may relay a valid answer, but nobody may set a price without a valid, authorized attestation.

3. Updates and freshness

Start with no price. Do not initialize the deployed contract with a hardcoded or simulated observation.

On a successful update, store the price, request ID, attestation issue time, expiry, onchain receipt time, and panel agreement information. Emit an event identifying the update.

Reject expired attestations, future-issued attestations, reused request IDs, and answers whose issue time is not strictly newer than the stored observation. Apply a maximum age of 24 hours from issuance.

Allow a newly signed observation to refresh the feed even when its price is unchanged.

Provide:
- A reader exposing the last stored observation and whether it is fresh.
- A strict price reader that reverts when there is no observation or it is stale.

Expiry must not erase history. Never renew freshness merely because someone reads the feed. Label issuance time accurately; it is not the date of the underlying card sales.

4. Deployment and scope

Keep the application minimal and non-upgradeable, with no manual price override or custody of user funds. Configure deployment parameters through constructors compatible with IMD’s factory. If an administrative role is necessary for question binding, use the requester’s $owner configuration, never the deploying factory’s msg.sender, and document its powers.

Follow IMD’s required launch-token rules if the selected deployment route requires a LaunchToken. The card-price feed must operate independently of that token and its pool.

A website, watcher, recurring scheduler, automated relayer, and paid oracle requests are outside this assignment. Leave the deployed feed ready for us to submit real attestations afterward.

5. Tests and delivery

Provide meaningful Foundry tests for two successive valid updates, an unchanged-price refresh, unauthorized signers, wrong question, wrong domain/chain, insufficient agreement, malformed data, expiry, future timestamps, replay, out-of-order updates, and empty/stale reads. Include a small test consumer demonstrating another contract reading the price. Keep test signatures and fixtures separate from the deployed configuration.

Deliver the source repository, passing test results, independent review, ABI, deployed Sepolia address, and deployment transaction.

Include a beginner-readable README and a reusable oracle-request template specifying the exact question, cents denomination, panel evidence, panel size 20, quorum 14, zero numeric tolerance, 24-hour validity, and the deployed consumer configuration.

Include a small utility that takes IMD’s actual attestation API response and prepares the contract update calldata. Document how to submit it with an external wallet; never request or embed private keys.

Clearly distinguish locally tested behavior from live verification. Do not claim the live price integration has succeeded until a real IMD attestation has actually been accepted onchain.

Deliver the actual finished MP4, not just a script. This is a fresh production.

CREATIVE DIRECTION
Clean, playful, confident product motion design with the official Pepe2Pepe characters. Make matching a bet feel understandable and satisfying. One coherent visual story, with beautifully timed animation and a memorable ending. Quiet instrumental music and a few soft matching/refund sound effects. ABSOLUTELY NO voiceover, narration, spoken words, singing, or text-to-speech. All meaning must work with sound off. Avoid a static slideshow, repetitive zooms, generic stock footage, flashing neon, tiny captions, and rushed title cards. Allow captions time to be read. Do not use robotic narration from earlier videos.

BRAND AND SOURCES
Inspect https://pepe2pepe.fun and https://pepe2pepe.fun/guide for the visual identity. Official hero artwork: https://pepe2pepe.fun/brand/pepe2pepe-v2.png . Optional official face: https://pepe2pepe.fun/brand/pepe-face.png . Download public assets into the workspace first when needed; media commands use local relative paths. Use the existing two hooded Pepe characters / YES and NO identity, midnight navy/teal backgrounds, mint accents, restrained lilac/coral accents, and crisp pale typography. Prefer Barlow Condensed for large headings and Space Grotesk for readable labels if available. Build an original animated composition around real brand assets, not a recording of clicking around the website. Do not access wallets or place bets.

STORYBOARD (you may refine pacing and wording while preserving the mechanics)
0–4s: Hero brand entrance. A good hook: “Your take. Someone else's other side.” Official characters face a clean YES / NO market card. Show pepe2pepe.fun clearly.
4–10s: “Back a side. Set the challenge.” Bring two YES backers into one visible queue. Earlier backing appears first, later backing second. Label the example “Illustration · 50/50 odds · fees excluded”. Use simple illustrative token units, NOT real trading-volume figures: first backer deposits 6, second deposits 4.
10–18s: “The other side makes the match.” Opposing NO stake of 8 flows in. Show exactly 6 of the first backing and 2 of the later backing lighting up as matched; leave the last 2 visibly unfilled. Keep the diagram consistent across shots. Match 8 YES with 8 NO: 16 funded units in the example. Earlier backing matches first. No chart implying price appreciation.
18–25s: “Matched stakes fund the payout.” Show that both sides' matched funds are already locked in; after a YES result in this illustration, the winning matched positions receive the combined matched stakes. At these equal odds: first YES backer's 6 has a gross payout of 12; later YES backer's matched 2 has a gross payout of 4. You can visualize this without extra number clutter. The losing NO matched stake loses; payout does not depend on future customers or later deposits. Keep the example/fees qualifier readable.
25–31s: “Not fully matched? Reclaim what's unused.” Highlight the remaining 2 of the later YES backing and return it along a separate refund arrow after the market's betting window closes. Required readable qualifier: “Claim after close. Fees apply.” This is a claim/refund right, not an automatic instant transfer. Do not promise a fee-free full refund, winnings on unmatched backing, or zero risk. A backer may be partly matched; only their matched portion participates in the result.
31–37s: An understated but upbeat launch snapshot: “13 markets created” and “789 active users”. Label the user metric “Google Analytics snapshot”. No volume figures, fee-revenue figures, trading totals, or invented growth percentages. Present the two numbers with elegant count-up or clean reveals, not a wall of metrics. If space allows, a separate short line may say “No major hiccups reported in our first four days” (a founder-reported launch update, not an audit/security claim). Do NOT claim the 789 users were measured in four days: the supplied analytics screenshot does not show its date range. Favor legibility over cramming in this optional line.
37–42s: Beautiful branded finish held long enough to read: “Take the other side.” and “pepe2pepe.fun”. Small supporting “Powered by the IMD Oracle” is allowed; do not claim fully automatic settlement, independent audits, guaranteed returns, or guaranteed security.

FACTUAL GUARDRAILS
This product uses funded FIXED-ODDS offers with FIFO backing, not pari-mutuel odds that change as people join. Use the 50/50 example only as an explicitly labeled illustration; other markets can have different fixed odds. A later deposit never jumps earlier backing in the queue. Unused backing is claimable after betting closes and can carry an unmatched fee; it does not have to wait for the oracle outcome. Matched winnings do wait for resolution and must be claimed. Fees and gas can apply. The example numbers are illustrative stake units, not business KPIs. The user specifically chose to leave dollar-volume and revenue stats OUT of this video.

ANALYTICS SOURCE FOR PRODUCTION NOTES
The owner supplied a Google Analytics report screenshot on 2026-10-02. It displays: Active users 789; New users 796; Average engagement time per active user 1m 01s; Event count 5.8K. The date range is cropped out. Only show the 789 active-user number in the film; the other figures are source context. Events are NOT bets, trades, transactions, visits or pageviews; active users are NOT verified traders or wallet holders. Do not add active and new users together. “13 markets created” is the owner's reported launch statistic, not an independently audited count. Do not send private analytics screenshots to third-party media providers.

the contracts are for

PepesFamily is a token launchpad on Robinhood Chain (chain ID 4663), built on Uniswap v4.

Anyone can launch a token with a fixed supply of 1B, paired with ETH or IMD.
At launch, the whole supply becomes single-sided liquidity in a new v4 pool. The launchpad contract owns that position and has no way to remove it, so liquidity is locked forever.
The launchpad is also the pool's v4 hook. It takes 4% of the quote side of every swap, through any router: 1% to the protocol, and 3% to the token's holders pro rata, which they claim.
Tokens have no mint, no owner (owner() returns 0x0 in v2) and no admin functions. Nothing is upgradeable.
The launchpad owner can only change where the protocol fee goes and the starting price for future launches.
Contracts

v2 (current):
PepesFamily.sol: launcher, hook, fee vault
PadToken.sol: the launched ERC-20, with holder rewards and EIP-2612 permit
PepesFamilyRouter.sol
PepesFamilyEthRouter.sol: trades IMD pairs with ETH via the v4 IMD/ETH pool
lib/SafeTransfer.sol
deploy scripts
v1 (still live with real liquidity): src/v1/PadTokenV1.sol, plus the v1 launchpad and routers at commit a549093. The main difference from v2: the v1 router can pull tokens without an allowance, but only from its own caller.
About 1,340 lines of Solidity in total. Uniswap v4-core is out of scope.
What to look at hardest

Hook fee accounting: delta signs for exact-in and exact-out in both currency orders; the transient-storage handoff between beforeSwap and afterSwap; fees on partially filled swaps.
Fee claims and payouts: fees are held as Uniswap claim balances and paid out by flush and collectProtocolFees. Anyone can call those while the pool manager is mid-transaction for another contract. Can that ever drain the pool manager or break our accounting?
Launch liquidity math: rounding, both token orderings, extreme starting prices.
Holder reward accounting: overflow bounds, the excluded-address list, reentrancy on claim, and that payouts can never exceed what was distributed.
Permit and the routers: EIP-712 correctness, front-run handling, msg.value and refunds, the two-swap ETH route.
The v1 router's approval shortcut: confirm nobody can move another holder's tokens. GoPlus flags v1 tokens as a honeypot because of it, and we believe that's a false positive.
Invariants to verify

Liquidity can never be removed.
Every swap pays exactly 4%.
Fee claims and reward payouts are always fully backed.
Supply is fixed.
Routers only spend the caller's funds.
Nobody can block selling or claiming.
